did: Home now fetches the public pages a cards essay shows, the way it fetches snips. Each mailbox pass finds the Public Pages Capture run that a page scene names, downloads that run's one-day bundle, checks it whole, and hands the essay's pages beside it to the render as pages.json and the pictures. The snips fetcher was made general over two kinds of bundle rather than copied, so both share one queue, one set of limits and one deadline. A scene whose run doesn't hold its picture at the same address and moment is refused page-gone. With no token, or a run or file no capture makes, it is refused page-missing. Run again on Studio re-checks both.

calls.title: Pages share the snips fetcher and its limits
options: One fetcher over snips and pages, one queue, at most five lookups and one download a pass in all
A second fetcher copied for pages
The shared fetcher with separate limits for each kind
calls.why: The brief asked for the family rather than a copy, and shared limits keep the mailbox pass from waiting any longer than it did before.
calls.undo: Give each family its own limits in snips.rs run_once (C1440 in server docs/snips.md).

calls.title: Pages go first in the shared queue
options: Pages before snips among keys never looked at and keys marked gone, with failed keys taking turns oldest first
calls.why: A pages bundle lives one day and can't be made again, and the pass runs hourly with one download, so a day of snips could outlive it. Always-first let a failing page starve snips.
calls.undo: Drop Family::first from the sort key in snips.rs (C1443).

calls.title: A capture still running waits instead of being refused
options: Only retry a run not yet finished, and let a newer attempt under way clear an old gone mark
Mark a run not yet finished as gone, like one that failed
calls.why: ESSAY-Q2 asked for it: Studio's page-gone words tell the owner to capture again, which is wrong for a run about to succeed.
calls.undo: Map a null conclusion to no run in OneRun::of_pages (C1442).

left: An essay taken back before its video is made loses its pages folder, and if a day passes before it is given again it is refused page-gone; keeping the pictures longer would be a library, which the owner ruled out.
A run already fetched is not fetched again for a newer attempt, so a cut list naming the newer attempt's pictures is refused page-gone; the recovery is a new capture.
A capture run that never finishes is asked about every pass until GitHub ends it, and its essay waits that long.
The assurance ledger's CE1 entry for pages is ESSAY-Q2's some-ui PR, not this session's.
